title: Three sine pairs reduce fitted dip asymmetry but worsen local predictions for KIC 11084727 in Kepler quarter 11
abstract: We tested the known dip of KIC 11084727 in Kepler release 25 quarter 11. Three sine and cosine pairs reduce the fitted exit-to-entry width ratio. However, they increase local held-out prediction error by factors of 5.33 in aperture flux and 2.11 in corrected flux. Frequencies for this check are selected outside the full validation window. The exit remains longer in all 24 tested joint fits. Its size depends strongly on baseline treatment. For the reference corrected-flux fit with sine pairs, a conditional 95 percent residual-block interval is 1.18 to 2.47. This test does not identify stellar periods, dust, or a new body. Both flux products use the same observations. Instrument effects, source blends, baseline error, and time-dependent noise remain possible. No independent telescope observation is used. The package includes the exact FITS input, hashes, code, all fits and resampling draws, prediction tests, figures, and offline instructions.
